HANDBOOK WALK-THROUGH

Make one ribbon connection

  1. Seat the inert sample. Rotate the holder until the ordered pad pair lines up with the feed arrow, then move the first pad under the wedge. The example starts aligned at 90°.
  2. Hold the Multi Mouse control at first search. Fine-align if needed, then release to make the first virtual bond.
  3. At loop height, move the stage to the second pad. Hold for second search and release. The virtual wedge returns to reset, with a new assembly revision only if the route clears the keep-out.

Try a 120 µm loop for a blocked route, then 160 µm for the passing case. The new JSON preserves the stable pad IDs, the wire path, and the assembly revision. It is not a machine recipe.

Evidence, dimensions and simulation limits
Manufacturer sequence§6.1.1, pp. 6-1 to 6-3. Hold for first search, release, move manually to the second pad at loop, hold and release again. Right-hand 4523D, not the AD motorized variant.
Envelope / spool680 × 700 × 530 mm nominal W × D × H. The vertical feed uses a 50.8 mm head-mounted reel. Housing contours and internal dimensions not given are inferred.
Motion14 mm total fine travel, 6:1 table-to-mouse reduction and 6.6 mm nominal low reset. Simulator uses 90 µm search (manual §4.3.2.2.1: 75–100 µm). Swing geometry, clamp travel, animation times, and fine alignment threshold are modeled, not measured.
Inputbts.wedge-pad-map.v1. Flat pads with stable IDs and intended nets, keep-out boxes, package-local coordinates in µm, and input revision. This holder supports pads inside a 3.6 mm region and 70–400 µm illustrative loop settings.
Outputbts.wedge-assembly.v1. Pad/net IDs, nominal contact coordinates, finite ribbon envelope, minimum geometric gap and assembly revision with only accepted edges. Contact centers are nominal after alignment passes. This does not predict metallurgical quality, strength, contact resistance, or measured continuity.

The rebuilt instrument against the references

Four renders of the editable workshop model, paired with views of the real instrument. The camera angles are approximate, not a photographic registration.

  • Front-left: controls on the correct sides

    The open-front base, left LCD, right hand control and raised workholder match the layout. The modeled housing is boxier and its panel is less steeply inclined.

    KTH front-left photograph
  • Front-right: optics, lamp and specimen area

    The head overhangs the stage and has a distinct inclined light near the binoculars. The authored microscope and teaching fixture are not exact copies of the KTH accessories.

    KTH front-right photograph
  • Operator view: six function keys, separate keypad

    The right temperature display sits to the left of six controls (two rows of three); the left keypad has cursor and three trim pairs. Keycap outlines are simplified.

    KTH panel and Multi Mouse
  • Side: optional head-mounted ribbon spool

    The large vertical spool is carried above the head arm, above a separate transducer terminating in a vertical tool. Clamp proportions, wedge profile and working offsets are inferred.

    K&S Fig. 5-13, accessory side view

Photographs of the 4523D at KTH

Institutional documentation: Albanova Nano-Fab-Lab, KTH / Stockholm University. Use both angles for handedness and fixture context.

  • KTH 0775 · complete station, operator’s left

    4523D, right-hand controls, round-wire setup. The key pad is in the left wing; binoculars look down past the head onto the holder, with a shallow cutaway in the front base.

  • KTH 0777 · complete station, operator’s right

    Same KTH installation, opposite oblique. Shows the right mouse well, inclined head illumination and broad workholder in their operating context.

  • KTH 0778 · tool and fixture, left

    Transducer nose, clamp, downward wedge and metal fixture insert. Two clamp plates fix the sample to the rectangular insert within a round workholder; this is one facility accessory, not universal.

  • KTH 0780 · tool and fixture, right

    Opposing close-up distinguishes a spring/clamping fixture and raised rim from the moving table below. Use for shape/relationships, not dimensions.

  • KTH 0782 · operator keypad

    On this right-hand 4523D the left-side keypad has a program row, cursor cluster, and separate paired search/loop/tail trim keys. Rear panel in this photograph is the upright operator-facing LCD fascia, not the rear of the instrument.

  • KTH 0783 · right panel and Multi Mouse

    Left half of upright panel: temperature controller. Right half: six function keys arranged 3 across × 2 rows; handheld controller below has divided top and dark side button.

  • KTH 0784 / 0785 · holder side, two directions

    Opposing side views show concentric support levels, a textured rim or grip, base and locking/height hardware; the exact fixture at KTH differs from an idealized coupon carrier.

Additional image: opposing holder side, KTH 0785.

Manufacturer’s illustrated handbook

Kulicke & Soffa, 4500 Digital Series Manual Wire Bonders: Operations and Maintenance Manual, March 2002, P/N 94500-000D-000-01. The figure links open the original published document.

  • K&S Figs. 3-1, 3-2 · chassis and head

    March 2002 4500 series, printed 3-1–3-2. Whole-machine figure is a family illustration; use top subfigure on the next page for the wedge head. The lower figure is a different ball-bonder family.

  • K&S Figs. 4-2, 4-3 · mouse and right panel

    Printed 4-2–4-3. Identifies left pushbutton (Semi/Auto), right pushbutton (Stitch), thumb control (Manual Z); wedge-model right panel is on next page.

  • K&S Fig. 5-2 · wedge orientation

    Printed 5-2, lower photo only. A vertical feed option on the 4523D/AD, distinct from the angled-feed example above it. This photo includes a temporary gauge; that gauge is not part of a loaded sample.

  • K&S Fig. 5-12 · vertical ribbon assembly from front

    Printed 5-21, lower photo. Head and spotlight are separate; a two-inch ribbon spool is on the head, and the operator-facing connector cluster is below the head.

  • K&S Fig. 5-13 · side of vertical ribbon head

    Printed 5-22. Side photo isolates the large pale spool above the long head lever; parallel lower transducer descends to a slender wedge at the nose. More useful for our selected feed than KTH’s round-wire images.

  • K&S Figs. 9-1 to 9-3 · inside left/right of main head

    Printed 9-3–9-5. Housing removed; these views explain the fixed pivot, rotating bonding head and adjacent lifters. Not an external rear view.

Limits of the reconstruction

The published envelope is 680 × 700 × 530 mm (W × D × H). The 2-inch spool is nominally 50.8 mm in diameter. The unmeasured housing contours, bracket offsets and teaching fixture are inferred, not digitized. Both rear fuses are documented (p. 8-1), but no photograph here establishes their rear-panel coordinates.

Source photographs are linked, not redistributed. No photographic or manual pixels are embedded in the original schematics.
